question_text:
Passage: The Gender and Development (GAD) budget policy mandates that all government agencies allocate at least five percent of their total budget appropriations to programs and projects that address gender issues and promote women's empowerment. This allocation, known as the GAD budget, is intended to ensure that gender concerns are integrated into the mainstream planning and budgeting processes of agencies. The policy also requires agencies to submit a GAD Accomplishment Report annually to the Philippine Commission on Women (PCW) and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).

What can be inferred about the purpose of the GAD budget policy?

options.text: It aims to reduce the overall budget of agencies.
It seeks to make gender concerns a regular part of agency planning.
It requires agencies to prioritize women's projects over all others.
It only applies to agencies with large budgets.
